reuse.why: The rule is changed inside the existing shared getExpectedAmount/getScheduledAmount helpers and the approximate tolerance reuses getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules, and the budget template that had its own midpoint arithmetic now calls the helper too; but the template keeps its own op dispatch instead of passing op straight through.

duplication.why: No new copies of the arithmetic; the only residual duplication is schedule-template's own 'isbetween || isapprox ? helper : value' branch, which repeats the dispatch getExpectedAmount already does.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount, and the API field is computed in the existing scheduleModel mapper in api-models.ts.

scope.why: Focused on the four steps, but it leaves stale 'rounded midpoint' comments at the call sites and a release note that still describes the step-1 'furthest from zero' rule.

maintainability.why: Making op an optional trailing parameter means callers that omit it (the desktop getScheduledAmount callers, and getScheduledAmount(x, false, op) in the API) silently skip the approximate rule, so whether the rule applies depends on each caller remembering to pass op.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All touched server sites go through getExpectedAmount/getScheduledAmount; schedule-template wraps the helper in its own op ternary rather than bypassing it.

disguised_duplication.where: The only repeat is the visible op ternary in server/budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList; it is not renamed or reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: An optional op parameter was added to getExpectedAmount and threaded through getScheduledAmount (2), with an 'isapprox' branch inside getExpectedAmount (1); schedule-template.ts keeps its own op dispatch around the helper, and desktop-client getScheduledAmount callers (SchedulesTable, Balance, mobile list) do not pass op.
